_about: Each traced ground's boundary line as the match plays it (tools/grounds/boundary/fit_boundary.py). frame: [x, z, degrees] in the model's glb metres: the goals' midpoint and the line through them. boundary/fence: r(t) = a0 + sum(a_k cos kt + b_k sin kt) about that midpoint, t from the +x goal towards +y (the glb's +z after the turn).

cazalys.source: Google Earth 3D top-down captures (2026-11-22), GE pinhole geometry calibrated on the 50 m centre square (50.0 m). line: centre of the painted boundary ridge, one point per 2 m window, 320 windows on 16 tiles round the ground. goals: middle of each goal line between the goal-post bases (shadow roots) on two d=95 m top-downs. centre: midpoint of the two goals, NOT a measured centre circle. fence: fence base, 2 m windows (shadow-corrected), kept points of the 0.32 m rms ellipse fit.

gmhba.source: Google Earth 3D, close straight-down shots (130 m camera) stitched; tile set gem (Google Earth's current 3D imagery, viewed 2026-11-22), about 0.08 m pixels. AFL markings visible. Ten straight-down Google Earth shots from a ~130 m camera round the boundary, stitched into one east/north picture at 0.08 m. Painted line traced as the ridge of a thin bright line with lit grass 1.5 m either side, along 1440 rays, then a 12-term Fourier radius about the centre fitted to the points seen. Goals: middle of the goal line from a 6.4 x 9 m goal-square template, checked against the 50 m arcs. Centre: 50 m centre square + 10 m circle template.

trace_error.placement_on_google_earth: Google Earth itself (the frame the GMHBA origin was solved in from 7 GE wall-foot points); camera heights read off GE's status bar to 1 m (about 0.7% in scale); the 50 m arcs come out at 49.7 and 50.2 m
